narrative.headline: Hims: FTC Data-Privacy Lawsuit Signals Subscription-Disclosure Compliance Exposure
narrative.body: Hims operates a multi-category consumer telehealth platform with significant exposure to state asynchronous prescribing rules and compounded GLP-1 supply-chain dependency, making subscription-disclosure and user-data governance material operational risks. The most recent 10-K names state telehealth licensing variance and FDA enforcement on compounded GLP-1 products as disclosed risks. An FTC lawsuit alleging incomplete user-data and subscription-cancellation disclosures creates direct precedent for state attorneys general and pharmacy boards to audit similar compliance gaps across California, New York, and Florida operations. Hims' government affairs team should assess whether current subscription-disclosure language and data-handling practices align with emerging state privacy standards and FTC guidance on telehealth consumer protection.

narrative.headline: LifeMD: California Telehealth Data Practice Faces FTC Enforcement Precedent
narrative.body: LifeMD operates a consumer-direct GLP-1 platform with asynchronous prescribing and subscription models, creating material exposure to FTC data-practice enforcement similar to the Hims litigation filed in 2026. The most recent 10-K names state telehealth prescribing restrictions and pharmacy oversight as material risks, and California's AG office has historically pursued aggressive enforcement on telehealth subscription cancellation practices. LifeMD's government affairs team should assess whether current user data handling, subscription retention mechanics, or state-specific disclosures require defensibility review against the emerging FTC enforcement baseline. The composite regulatory and reputational exposure is highest in California, Florida, and Texas given compounded GLP-1 supply-chain and prescribing-authority variance.
